name: UC3854BDWTR
title: Power-factor-correction preregulator controller
summary: An average-current-mode controller working at fixed frequency, for a boost power-factor-correction preregulator, pin compatible with the older UC3854. It holds the line current in step with the line voltage through a multiplier, a low-offset current amplifier of 5 MHz and a voltage amplifier with soft-start, and adds a 1 % 7.5 V reference, an oscillator, line feedforward through a VRMS squarer, a supply clamp, a peak current comparator and a totem-pole gate driver of 1.5 A peak. The A versions start at 16 V for off-line use, the B versions at 10.5 V for an auxiliary 12 V supply.
key_figures: fixed-frequency average current mode, boost PFC
10 V to 20 V recommended, 22 V absolute
A: 16 V / 10 V typ; B: 10.5 V / 10.3 V typ
5 MHz typ gain-bandwidth, offset –4 mV to 0 mV at 25 °C
100 kHz typ at RT = 8.2 kΩ, CT = 1.5 nF
1.5 A peak (50 % duty), 35 ns rise/fall into 1 nF

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground and voltage reference point. Bypass and timing capacitors go to this pin by short, direct leads.

pins.name: PKLMT
pins.function: Peak current limit input with a 0.0 V threshold. Connect it to the negative end of the current-sense resistor and pull it up to REF through a resistor so the negative sense voltage is shifted up to ground.

pins.name: CAO
pins.function: Current amplifier output, one input of the PWM duty-cycle comparator; it commands the PWM so the input current follows its programme. Swings from 0.1 V to 7.5 V.

pins.name: ISENSE
pins.function: Current amplifier – input, where the switch current is sensed. Works down to and below ground; diodes to GND protect it, so keep it above –0.5 V.

pins.name: MOUT
pins.function: Multiplier output, joined inside to the current amplifier's + input. Since the multiplier delivers a current, this node is high impedance, as ISENSE is, which lets the current amplifier be wired differentially so ground noise cancels. Keep it above –0.5 V. IMOUT ≤ 2 × IAC.

pins.name: IAC
pins.function: Multiplier input taking a current that follows the momentary line voltage. The path from IAC to MOUT is the one built for low distortion, so line-voltage waveform sensing belongs on this pin and on no other multiplier input.

pins.name: VAO
pins.function: Voltage amplifier output, the third multiplier input; clamped internally to 6.0 V.

pins.name: VRMS
pins.function: Multiplier input that carries the RMS line voltage.

pins.name: VREF
pins.function: 7.5 V reference output; sets the peak-limit point and biases internal circuits. The device does not run unless this voltage is present.

pins.name: ENA
pins.function: Enable. The device starts once the pin rises above 2.65 V nominal and stops when it falls below 2.15 V nominal. Clamped internally near 10 V.

pins.name: VSENSE
pins.function: Voltage amplifier inverting input, fed from the output voltage; its error amplifier output is a multiplier input.

pins.name: RSET
pins.function: A resistor to ground sets the oscillator charging current.

pins.name: SS
pins.function: Soft-start. Kept at GND while disabled or while VCC is under UVLO; when VCC is good and ENA is high, an internal 14 µA source charges it to over 3 V. While SS is below the reference it serves as the voltage amplifier reference, so a large capacitor to GND ramps the reference and the duty cycle slowly. A disable or a supply dropout discharges it quickly and stops the PWM.

pins.name: CT
pins.function: A capacitor to GND sets the oscillator frequency.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Positive supply.

pins.name: GTDRV
pins.function: Gate drive output, a 1.5 A peak totem pole for a MOSFET. Put 5 Ω or more in series with the gate to stop the gate impedance and the driver interacting and overshooting badly; some overshoot always occurs into a capacitive load.

pins.name: N/C
pins.function: Not connected.

operation.text: The controller makes a boost stage draw a line current whose shape matches the line voltage, for near-unity power factor and under 3 % current distortion without range switching. It uses fixed-frequency average current-mode control, which keeps the sinusoidal current stable and low in distortion without the slope compensation that peak current mode needs.

Pin compatible with the UC3854 and its replacement. Added or changed: a wider-band, lower-offset current amplifier; a quicker and more accurate enable comparator; a reference-good comparator; two UVLO choices; lower start-up current; a better multiply/divide circuit; output clamps on both amplifiers; stronger amplifier current sinking; and an IAC pin at low offset voltage. The MOUT/current amplifier input common-mode range is wider, giving more freedom in how current is sensed.
The A versions turn on at 16 V and off at 10 V, for off-line start-up. The B versions turn on at 10.5 V and off at 10 V, so they can run from an auxiliary 12 V regulator.

The gain constant is the same as the UC3854's (K = –1 /V). IAC is held at 500 mV nominal over the full temperature range instead of 6.0 V, so no zero-crossing compensation resistor from IAC to VREF is needed. Limit the IAC current at high line to 250 µA for best performance.

VRMS works linearly from 0 V to 5.5 V. The squarer is a true analog multiplier, not a piecewise approximation, so it is more accurate and has no discontinuities. Size the VRMS divider for 1.5 V at 85 VAC low line; at 270 VAC high line VRMS is then 4.77 V.

operation.topic: Multiplier, VAO input and output range
operation.text: The voltage amplifier output is clamped internally to 6.0 V, so the outside zener clamp used with the UC3854 is not needed; the multiplier offset on this input is 1.5 V. MOUT, which is also the current amplifier + input, swings over a range of –0.3 V to 5.0 V (the UC3854's was –0.3 V to 2.5 V), which suits large current-sense signals.

RSET sets only the oscillator charging current; it no longer clamps the multiplier output. The multiplier output current is clamped at 2 × IAC at all times, which gives foldback power limiting in brownout and at very low line.

Its reference is the 3 V internal level, lower than the UC3854's, so the compensation capacitors hold less charge and recover faster after line dropouts or interruptions, and less dc current flows in the feedback network. The output has a 6.0 V temperature-compensated clamp and an active pull-down transistor, and its short-circuit current is 2 mA typical.

Low offset keeps line current distortion low. The offset is negative, so with a zero current command (both inputs at zero) the PWM does not drive the MOSFET and no outside offset-cancelling network is needed. Bandwidth is 5 MHz typical, which matters for 400 Hz avionics supplies more than for 50 Hz or 60 Hz lines.
VCC is clamped at 20 V, so the controller may be fed from a current source. Start-up current is 250 µA typical, which cuts the dissipation of an off-line start-up resistor.

The gate driver output stays low until the supply and the 7.5 V reference are up, so the Schottky diodes some UC3854 designs put on PKLMT and MOUT are not needed. Propagation delay of the disable is 300 ns typical; on the UC3854 it depended on the VREF capacitor and was orders of magnitude longer.

ENA above 2.65 V nominal lets the device start; once running it shuts off if ENA drops below 2.15 V nominal. Threshold 2.55 V typical with 500 mV typical hysteresis. ENA is clamped internally near 10 V.

SS sits at ground while the part is disabled or VCC is below UVLO. When both are good, a 14 µA source charges the SS capacitor past 3 V; until it reaches the reference, SS acts as the voltage amplifier reference, so the output reference and the duty cycle rise slowly. A disable or supply dropout discharges SS quickly and turns the PWM off.

PKLMT trips at 0.0 V. It is connected to the negative side of the current-sense resistor and offset upward with a resistor to REF, so the negative sense signal reaches ground at the chosen peak current.

Totem-pole output, 1.5 A peak. 5 Ω or more between GTDRV and the gate keeps the gate impedance from interacting with the driver and causing excessive overshoot; a capacitive load always gives some overshoot.

ISENSE and MOUT keep working down to and below ground but are clamped by diodes to GND, so they must not go below –0.5 V. MOUT is a high-impedance current node, which allows a differential current amplifier connection that cancels ground noise.
Bypass and timing capacitors returned to GND need short, direct leads.
ESD protection is limited: store and handle the parts with the leads shorted together or in conductive foam.
